title: Incorporate KV-cache stall mitigation and operator watchlist into Serving PRD
creator: Anika Patel
description: Summary: Following the KV-cache stall incident on 2026-01-28 (INC-2026-045), this ticket captures the product requirements and acceptance criteria to encode the incident action items into the Serving PRD. Goal: reduce customer-visible request stalls caused by KV-cache regen and long-running cache eviction cycles, and provide operators with a clear watchlist, SLO guardrails, and deterministic rollback triggers. These PRD-level changes will be scoped to runtime-2.4 and the Console UI for operator workflows. This ticket includes: (1) functional requirements for runtime behavior changes (graceful stall mitigation, progressive backoff, safe cache regen), (2) operator-facing watchlist and Runbook entries surfaced in Console, (3) acceptance tests and synthetic scenarios for verification, and (4) rollout gating and rollback criteria integrated into release checklists.
acceptance_criteria: Runtime will detect KV-cache regeneration stalls and trigger a low-latency fallback path within 150ms of stall detection for high-priority routes; verified by end-to-end synthetic test (p99 tail latency improvement >20% during regeneration window)
Operator Console will expose a Watchlist card that surfaces nodes experiencing >3 cache-regen failures in 10m, with a one-click drilldown to recent logs and the related incident postmortem link
Rollout gating: Canary must run for at least 6 hours in two regions with traffic shaping enabled; no more than 1 minor SLO breach attributable to cache-related stalls during canary to proceed to ramp

Automated rollback trigger: If percentage of requests using fallback path exceeds 15% for a sustained 10-minute window in production during ramp, deployment automatically pauses and notifies on-call with remediation play
Synthetic acceptance harness: Add a KV-cache regen chaos test to CI that reproduces the incident pattern and verifies the fallback path maintains p95 latency under the threshold defined in SLOs
Documentation: PRD must include updated operator Runbook steps (detect, isolate, heal), list of relevant dashboards, and a migration note for Dedicated customers about config knob defaults
decisions: Fallback strategy: Use a prefixed request-level soft-cache bypass (temporary in-memory partial cache) rather than global cache reset to minimize throughput impact
Detection heuristic: Combine regeneration error rate with sustained increase in request KV miss latency to reduce false positives
Operator UX: Integrate watchlist into existing Console 'Health' tab rather than creating a new top-level view to reduce cognitive overhead
Rollout policy: Enforce progressive ramping with automatic pause/rollback on predefined traffic and SLO signals rather than manual gating only
scope_changes: Original PRD requested a generic 'cache health dashboard' — replaced with a focused Watchlist and Runbook integration scoped to KV-cache regeneration scenarios
Removed: full rework of cache eviction policy (moved to follow-up epic PM-36011) — this ticket implements operational mitigations and fallback paths only
Added: CI synthetic test harness for KV-cache regen chaos and a canary traffic shaping configuration in the Console
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (Canary): Deploy runtime-2.4 canary to 5% traffic in us-west1 and eu-west1 with watchlist enabled; duration 6–12 hours
Phase 2 (Ramp): If canary passes synthetic and live checks, ramp to 30% over 24 hours with automated monitoring hooks
Phase 3 (GA): Full ramp to 100% with staggered region-by-region rollout and post-ramp verification window of 48 hours
Fallback: If automated rollback triggers, hold and run an emergency verification test, capture traces, and revert by GitHub PR to previous runtime image following rollback checklist
